description: This topic covers India's industrial development and mineral wealth. It is a highly crucial geographical and economic section for competitive exams, focusing on the distribution of resources and industrial landmarks.

sections.title: Basic Concepts of Minerals and Industries
sections.description: Fundamental terminology required to understand minerals and the industrial sectors of the economy.

key_concepts.explanation: A naturally occurring inorganic solid substance with a definite chemical composition and specific physical properties.
A naturally occurring rock or sediment that contains sufficient minerals with economically important elements, typically metals, that can be economically extracted from it.
The eight foundational industries that constitute the backbone of the Indian industrial infrastructure: Coal, Crude Oil, Natural Gas, Refinery Products, Fertilizers, Steel, Cement, and Electricity.

sections.title: Historical Development of Indian Industries
sections.description: Major milestones and foundational events in the history of the Indian industrial sector.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts, superlatives, and key data points frequently tested in competitive exams.

important_facts.fact: The Chhota Nagpur Plateau is famously called the 'Ruhr of India' due to its exceptionally rich and abundant mineral resources.
The cotton textile industry is the largest agro-based industry in India and serves as one of the largest sources of employment in the country.
India is one of the largest producers and exporters of Mica globally, with Andhra Pradesh standing as the leading producer state.
The Panna mines, located in the state of Madhya Pradesh, are renowned throughout India for being the primary source of diamond production.
Jamnagar in Gujarat is home to the world's largest grassroots oil refinery complex, which is owned and operated by Reliance Industries Limited.
